title: LGV Lemma 2×2: Lindström-Gessel-Viennot via Involution Bijection
description: Proves the 2×2 case of the Lindström-Gessel-Viennot (LGV) Lemma: the number of non-intersecting pairs of lattice paths equals the determinant of path count matrix. The crossing lemma is proved via column entry order analysis, and the Lindström involution provides a sign-reversing bijection between intersecting pairs. 0 axiom declarations (native_decide relies on Lean.ofReduceBool), 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The Lindström-Gessel-Viennot (LGV) Lemma (Lindström 1973, Gessel-Viennot 1985) is a fundamental tool in combinatorics that counts non-intersecting lattice path systems using determinants. The 2×2 case states: given sources A₁, A₂ and targets B₁, B₂, the number of non-intersecting path pairs (A₁→B₁, A₂→B₂) equals e(A₁,B₁)·e(A₂,B₂) - e(A₁,B₂)·e(A₂,B₁), where e(A,B) is the number of monotone lattice paths from A to B. This file provides a complete formal proof with a novel crossing lemma via column entry order analysis.
overview.problemStatement: Prove the 2×2 LGV Lemma: for source points A₁=(0,a₁), A₂=(0,a₂) with a₁<a₂ and target points B₁=(m,b₁), B₂=(m,b₂) with b₁<b₂, the number of non-intersecting path pairs (P₁:A₁→B₁, P₂:A₂→B₂) equals C(m+b₁-a₁, m)·C(m+b₂-a₂, m) - C(m+b₂-a₁, m)·C(m+b₁-a₂, m).
overview.text: Lattice paths are encoded as lists of Booleans (false = East, true = North). The key function northBeforeEast l k counts North steps before the k-th East step, giving the y-coordinate when entering column k. The Crossing Lemma (fully proved) shows that if P₁ enters the grid lower than P₂ but exits higher, they must share a lattice point — proved by tracking column entry order via a disjoint interval monotonicity argument. The Lindström involution swaps path tails at the first shared point, creating a sign-reversing bijection on intersecting pairs. The LGV formula follows by inclusion-exclusion.
overview.proofStrategy: Part I defines LPath (Bool list), step counts, and PathMN (paths with exactly m East and n North steps). Path count is proved via binomial coefficients. Part II develops northBeforeEast and colEntry. Part III proves nonIntersecting_entry_order (the column entry preservation lemma) by induction on columns. Part IV proves the Crossing Lemma. Part V develops visitedPoints, sharedPoints, posAfter infrastructure. Part VI defines swapAtPoint and proves its involutivity and path structure preservation. Part VII defines the Lindström involution and proves it is a bijection on intersecting pairs. Part VIII assembles lgv_lemma_2x2 and derives ballot formula + Vandermonde identity.
keyInsights: northBeforeEast is the key invariant: it tracks the y-coordinate at column boundaries and is monotone in k
Crossing Lemma proof: use induction on columns — P₁ enters each column lower than P₂, so if P₁ ends higher, they must cross somewhere
disjoint interval argument: if paths are non-intersecting, their visited y-ranges in each column are disjoint (intervals don't overlap)
Lindström involution: swapping at the first crossing point gives an involution on intersecting pairs, proving the determinant formula
swapAtPoint involutivity: swapping twice recovers the original pair — proved by showing the new first crossing point equals the original
LGV formula follows: |NI pairs| = |all pairs| - |intersecting pairs| = e(A₁,B₁)e(A₂,B₂) - |involution pairs with wrong targets| = determinant

**nonIntersecting_entry_order is the single-step induction engine**: the Crossing Lemma is just this lemma applied m times. The proof of entry_order itself uses a sharp disjoint interval argument — the midpoint of l₂'s column range falls inside l₁'s column range if the order inverts.

**pathSplitEquiv encodes Pascal structurally**: the equivalence pathType (m+1) (n+1) ≃ pathType m (n+1) ⊕ pathType (m+1) n directly reflects Pascal's identity at the type level, making path_count_eq_choose a clean double induction with no ad hoc enumeration.

**canonSharedPoint is the crux of Lindström injectivity**: the key property is that minSharedStepIdx is preserved under swapAtPoint — both the forward and backward images share the same canonical point. This makes the two injections mutually inverse without needing to track the full path structure.
prerequisites: Combinatorics: binomial coefficients, lattice paths, inclusion-exclusion
Ballot problem (Bertrand 1887) for the formula connection
Catalan numbers as a special case

mainTheorems.name: lgv_lemma_2x2
mainTheorems.statement: Under a₁≤a₂, b₁≤b₂, a₁≤b₁, a₂≤b₂, a₂≤b₁: (niPairCount m (b₁−a₁) (b₂−a₂) a₁ a₂ : ℤ) = lgvDet m a₁ b₁ a₂ b₂
mainTheorems.significance: The central result: the 2×2 Lindström–Gessel–Viennot lemma. The number of pairs of NON-intersecting monotone lattice paths from sources (a₁,a₂) to targets (b₁,b₂) equals a 2×2 determinant of binomial path counts. The archetypal instance of the determinant-counts-non-intersecting-paths principle.
mainTheorems.description: Proved fully symbolically (no native_decide): degenerate same-start/same-end cases reduce directly; the generic case subtracts the crossing pairs — counted by lindstrom_involution — from the total path-pair count.

mainTheorems.name: lindstrom_involution
mainTheorems.statement: card {non-non-intersecting pairs in pathType m n₁ × pathType m n₂} = card (pathType m n₁' × pathType m n₂')
mainTheorems.significance: The heart of the LGV proof: the Lindström (Gessel–Viennot) sign-reversing involution. Intersecting path pairs are put in bijection with unconstrained path pairs on the swapped target multiset by exchanging tails at the first crossing — this is what makes the off-diagonal determinant terms cancel.
mainTheorems.description: Proved by antisymmetry from two injections lindstromForward_injective and lindstromBackward_injective; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: lindstromForward_injective
mainTheorems.statement: The tail-swap map from crossing pairs to swapped-target pairs is injective
mainTheorems.significance: One half of the Lindström involution's bijectivity: swapping the tails of a crossing pair at its canonical first shared point is an injective operation. Together with the backward map it forces the two cardinalities to coincide.
mainTheorems.description: Uses the canonical minimal shared point (canonSharedPoint) and the swap involution's coordinate lemmas; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: lindstromBackward_injective
mainTheorems.statement: The inverse tail-swap map is injective
mainTheorems.significance: The complementary injection: every swapped-target path pair, being forced to cross (crossing_always_intersecting), swaps back injectively to a distinct intersecting pair. The second inequality in the card-antisymmetry argument.
mainTheorems.description: Relies on crossing_always_intersecting to guarantee the reverse swap is well-defined; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: crossing_lemma
mainTheorems.statement: If paths l₁,l₂ have equal east-length m, north-lengths n₁,n₂, starts y₁<y₂ and ends y₂+n₂ < y₁+n₁, then they are NOT non-intersecting
mainTheorems.significance: The geometric crossing principle: two monotone lattice paths whose start and end orders are reversed must intersect. This is the combinatorial engine that forces off-diagonal (order-reversing) path pairs to cross.
mainTheorems.description: Proved by a column-by-column induction on the entry heights (nonIntersecting_entry_order) contradicting the reversed endpoint order; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: crossing_always_intersecting
mainTheorems.statement: For Q₁ ∈ pathType m n₁', Q₂ ∈ pathType m n₂' with a₁<a₂ and a₂+n₂' < a₁+n₁', Q₁ and Q₂ intersect
mainTheorems.significance: The pathType-typed form of the crossing lemma used to power the backward injection: on the swapped-target sizes every path pair is forced to cross, so the involution is defined on the whole set.
mainTheorems.description: Reduces to crossing_lemma via the path-type length/count properties; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: path_count_eq_choose
mainTheorems.statement: Fintype.card (pathType m n) = Nat.choose (m + n) m
mainTheorems.significance: The foundational enumeration: the number of monotone lattice paths with m east and n north steps is the binomial coefficient C(m+n, m). Every determinant entry in the LGV lemma is an instance of this count.
mainTheorems.description: Proved by induction on m via an explicit path-recursion equivalence; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: vandermonde
mainTheorems.statement: Nat.choose (m + n) r = ∑ k ∈ range (r+1), Nat.choose m k * Nat.choose n (r − k)
mainTheorems.significance: The Vandermonde convolution identity, the combinatorial cornerstone linking binomial coefficients of a sum to a convolution of products. Underlies the multiplicativity of path counts across a dividing line.
mainTheorems.description: Derived from Mathlib's Nat.add_choose_eq and the antidiagonal sum reindexing; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: catalan_formula
mainTheorems.significance: The closed form for the Catalan numbers Cₙ = C(2n,n)/(n+1), stated multiplicatively to stay within ℕ. Catalan numbers count balanced ballot sequences, Dyck paths, and non-crossing structures — the combinatorial family the whole entry orbits.
mainTheorems.description: Cn n is defined as C(2n,n) − C(2n,n+1); the identity follows by binomial absorption. Axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: ballot_formula
mainTheorems.statement: q < p, 1≤p, 1≤q → ballotSeqCount p q * (p + q) = (p − q) * Nat.choose (p + q) p
mainTheorems.significance: Bertrand's Ballot Theorem: the number of ballot sequences in which candidate A (with p votes) stays strictly ahead of B (with q votes) is (p−q)/(p+q) · C(p+q, p). The classical result at the entry's namesake.
mainTheorems.description: Multiplicative form (avoiding division in ℕ); proved by binomial absorption identities. Axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: ballot_via_path_count
mainTheorems.statement: 1≤p, 1≤q, q
mainTheorems.significance: The reflection-principle derivation of the ballot count as a DIFFERENCE of two lattice-path counts — the combinatorial-bijective route that mirrors the LGV determinant's subtraction of crossing configurations.
mainTheorems.description: Rewrites both path counts to binomials via path_count_eq_choose and symmetry; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: catalan_eq_ballot
mainTheorems.significance: Identifies the Catalan numbers with a boundary case of the ballot count (p = n+1, q = n): the sequences where A stays ahead with exactly one extra vote are exactly the Dyck/Catalan configurations. Unifies the two combinatorial families of the entry.
mainTheorems.description: Immediate by unfolding both definitions with arithmetic simplification; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: lgvDet_nonneg
mainTheorems.statement: Under the LGV ordering hypotheses, 0 ≤ lgvDet m a₁ b₁ a₂ b₂
mainTheorems.significance: Combinatorial positivity: because the LGV determinant counts an actual (non-negative) number of non-intersecting path pairs, it is non-negative. A clean corollary showing the determinant's structural meaning.
mainTheorems.description: Rewrites the determinant as niPairCount via lgv_lemma_2x2, then uses non-negativity of a cast natural number; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: choose_symm_via_paths
mainTheorems.statement: Nat.choose (m + n) m = Nat.choose (m + n) n
mainTheorems.significance: Binomial symmetry proved bijectively: reflecting a lattice path across the diagonal (pathFlip) swaps its east and north step counts, giving C(m+n,m)=C(m+n,n) by an explicit equivalence rather than algebra.
mainTheorems.description: Uses path_count_eq_choose on both sides plus the pathFlipEquiv reflection bijection; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: swapAtPoint_involutive
mainTheorems.significance: The tail-swap operation at a shared lattice point is an involution — swapping tails twice restores the original pair. The self-inverse property that makes the Lindström map a genuine (sign-reversing) involution and not merely a bijection.
mainTheorems.description: Proved by list-surgery on the path prefixes/suffixes at the split index; axiom-free.

mainTheorems.name: total_identity_count
mainTheorems.statement: card (pathType m n₁ × pathType m n₂) counted as Nat.choose (m+n₁) m * Nat.choose (m+n₂) m
mainTheorems.significance: The total (unconstrained) path-pair count that the LGV subtraction starts from: the product of two binomial path counts, which is exactly the diagonal term of the determinant before the crossing pairs are removed.
mainTheorems.description: Product of two instances of path_count_eq_choose over the independent path factors; axiom-free.

conclusion.summary: A complete, axiom-free formalization of the 2×2 LGV Lemma with a novel proof of the Crossing Lemma via column entry order analysis. The Lindström involution is fully constructed and proved to be a sign-reversing bijection on intersecting path pairs. 142 theorems, 0 axiom declarations (native_decide relies on Lean.ofReduceBool), 0 sorries across 2922 lines.
conclusion.implications: The LGV Lemma is a cornerstone of algebraic combinatorics, used in proofs of the hook-length formula, Schur polynomial identities, and determinantal point processes. This formalization provides Lean 4 infrastructure for lattice path arguments that can be extended to the general LGV lemma (arbitrary path systems) and to applications in representation theory.

sections.title: Overview: The 2×2 LGV Lemma via Crossing
sections.summary: Imports and module docstring for the 2×2 Lindström–Gessel–Viennot lemma, which extends the 1D ballot reflection principle to planar lattice paths. These head lines introduce the crossing lemma (a discrete IVT: a path starting lower but ending higher must share a lattice point), the northBeforeEast column-entry function, and the complement-counting / Lindström-involution route to e(A₁,B₁)·e(A₂,B₂) − e(A₁,B₂)·e(A₂,B₁), before the LatticePathLGV namespace opens.
sections.mathContext: The 2×2 LGV lemma counts non-intersecting pairs of lattice paths as a 2×2 determinant of binomial path counts e(A,B)=C(dx+dy,dx). The engine is a 2D reflection principle: if P₁ enters each column below P₂ yet ends above it, monotonicity of the column-entry offset forces a shared lattice point (crossing lemma); swapping tails there is the sign-reversing involution. Machine-checked, with the example computations discharged by native_decide.

sections.title: Part I: Lattice Path Definitions and northBeforeEast
sections.summary: Defines LPath (Bool list), eastSteps/northSteps counts, pathType (m East, n North steps), and the key function northBeforeEast. Proves northBeforeEast_mono (monotone in k) and colEntry as the y-offset at column boundaries.
sections.mathContext: LPath = List Bool; false = East (+x), true = North (+y). northBeforeEast l k = #{j : j-th step is N, and fewer than k E steps precede it}. colEntry l k = northBeforeEast l (k-1) for k ≥ 1.

sections.title: Part IV: Crossing Lemma (2D Reflection Principle)
sections.summary: Proves the Crossing Lemma: if P₁ starts strictly lower (y₁ < y₂) but ends strictly higher (y₁+n₁ > y₂+n₂), they must share a lattice point. Uses induction on columns via nonIntersecting_entry_order (disjoint interval preservation).
sections.mathContext: Inductive invariant: non-intersecting → y₁ + colEntry(l₁, k) < y₂ + colEntry(l₂, k) for all k. Base: hstart. Step: nonIntersecting_entry_order. Contradiction at k=m: hend forces finalRange overlap.

sections.title: Part V–X: Path Count Formula and Ballot Theorem
sections.summary: Proves path_count_eq_choose: |pathType m n| = C(m+n, m). Defines ballotSeqCount and proves ballot_formula via absorption identity (b*p = a*q) and Pascal's rule. Includes native_decide verified examples.
sections.mathContext: |pathType m n| = C(m+n, m) by bijection with {0,1}^{m+n} subsets. Ballot formula: ballotSeqCount(p,q)*(p+q) = (p-q)*C(p+q,p) for q < p — proved via Nat.add_one_mul_choose_eq (absorption) + Nat.choose_succ_succ' (Pascal).

sections.title: Part XI–XVI: Lindström Involution Infrastructure
sections.summary: Constructs swapAtPoint (swap path suffixes at a shared lattice point), proves swapAtPoint_involutive via List.take_left/drop_left, and assembles the full Lindström involution on intersecting path pairs via lindstromForward_injective and lindstromBackward_injective.
sections.mathContext: swapAtPoint l₁ l₂ a₁ a₂ p = (l₁.take i ++ l₂.drop j, l₂.take j ++ l₁.drop i) where i = splitIdx a₁ p, j = splitIdx a₂ p. Involutivity: List.take_left + List.take_append_drop. Lindström involution: bijection between (A₁→B₁, A₂→B₂) intersecting pairs and (A₁→B₂, A₂→B₁) all pairs.

sections.title: Part XVII: LGV Lemma 2×2 and Non-Negativity
sections.summary: Proves lgv_lemma_2x2: |NI pairs| = det[e(Aᵢ,Bⱼ)]. Three cases: equal starts, equal ends, general (strict). General case: complement counting + Lindström involution + algebra. Corollary lgvDet_nonneg: determinant is non-negative since it equals a count.
sections.mathContext: |NI| = e(A₁,B₁)e(A₂,B₂) - e(A₁,B₂)e(A₂,B₁). Proof: ni_complement_count' gives |NI| = total - |Int|; lindstrom_involution gives |Int| = crossed total; algebra via omega + zify + ring gives the determinant formula.
